sections: An action against a changing surface

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Visual Actuation and Computer Use** in *Tool Calling* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Tool Calling, § Visual Actuation and Computer Use
blocks.md: Consider the staging-container restart scenario when an administrative web dashboard provides no programmatic API. A **computer-use tool** bridges this interface gap by rendering visual screenshots to the model and translating model-generated targets into synthetic mouse clicks, keystrokes, or scrolling gestures, the low-level input space pioneered in early web-agent research. Operating on raw pixels does not relax system invariants. While the model proposes an interaction based on an observed frame, the execution runtime retains responsibility for validating arguments, enforcing authorization, dispatching OS events, and interpreting observations.

questions.q: The section **Visual Actuation and Computer Use** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Capture and staging are separate budgets, so the adapter drains both pipes, enforces byte limits, and stages a head-and-tail view with a typed notice of what was omitted and a handle to the rest.

A logical operation ID names one intended effect across attempts, each attempt gets a fresh attempt ID, and the ID is safe only under an endpoint contract that binds it to caller, scope, and arguments.
Every proposed call, reads included, passes a deterministic host reference monitor that validates, authorizes, dispatches with outcome tracking, and shapes the observation.
Which descriptors the model sees each turn and how much work each tool does are design variables priced in context tokens and in cost per accepted task.
